verses.zh: 约书亚死后，以色列人求问耶和华说：「我们中间谁当首先上去攻击迦南人，与他们争战？」
verses.en: After Joshua died, the Israelites asked[NOTE:1] the Lord, “Who should lead the invasion against the Canaanites and launch the attack?”[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew verb translated “asked” (שָׁאַל, shaʾal) refers here to consulting the Lord through a prophetic oracle; cf. NAB “consulted.”
Heb “Who should first go up for us against the Canaanites to attack them?”

verses.zh: 耶和华说：「犹大当先上去，我已将那地交在他手中。」
verses.en: The Lord said, “The men of Judah should take the lead.[NOTE:1] Be sure of this! I am handing the land over to them.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Judah should go up.”

The Hebrew exclamation הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally, “Behold”), translated “Be sure of this,” draws attention to the following statement. The verb form in the following statement (a Hebrew perfect, indicating completed action from the standpoint of the speaker) emphasizes the certainty of the event. Though it had not yet taken place, the Lord speaks of it as a “done deal.”

verses.zh: 犹大对他哥哥西缅说：「请你同我到拈阄所得之地去，好与迦南人争战；以后我也同你到你拈阄所得之地去。」于是西缅与他同去。
verses.en: The men of Judah said to their relatives, the men of Simeon,[NOTE:1] “Invade our allotted land with us and help us attack the Canaanites.[NOTE:2] Then we[NOTE:3] will go with you into your allotted land.” So the men of Simeon went with them.
notes: Heb “Judah said to Simeon, his brother.”
Heb “Come up with me into our allotted land and let us attack the Canaanites.”
Heb “I.” The Hebrew pronoun is singular, agreeing with the collective singular “Judah” earlier in the verse. English style requires a plural pronoun here, however.

verses.zh: 犹大就上去；耶和华将迦南人和比利洗人交在他们手中。他们在比色击杀了一万人，
verses.en: The men of Judah attacked,[NOTE:1] and the Lord handed the Canaanites and Perizzites over to them. They killed 10,000 men at Bezek.
notes: Heb “Judah went up.”

verses.zh: 又在那里遇见亚多尼・比色，与他争战，杀败迦南人和比利洗人。
verses.en: They met[NOTE:1] Adoni-Bezek at Bezek and fought him. They defeated the Canaanites and Perizzites.
notes: Or “found.”

verses.zh: 亚多尼・比色逃跑；他们追赶，拿住他，砍断他手脚的大拇指。
verses.en: When Adoni-Bezek ran away, they chased him and captured him. Then they cut off his thumbs and big toes.

verses.zh: 亚多尼・比色说：「从前有七十个王，手脚的大拇指都被我砍断，在我桌子底下拾取零碎食物。现在　神按着我所行的报应我了。」于是他们将亚多尼・比色带到耶路撒冷，他就死在那里。
verses.en: Adoni-Bezek said, “Seventy kings, with thumbs and big toes cut off, used to lick up[NOTE:1] food scraps[NOTE:2] under my table. God has repaid me for what I did to them.”[NOTE:3] They brought him to Jerusalem,[NOTE:4] where he died.
notes: Elsewhere this verb usually carries the sense of “to gather; to pick up; to glean,” but “lick up” seems best here in light of the peculiar circumstances described by Adoni-Bezek.
The words “food scraps” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied.
Heb “Just as I did, so God has repaid me.” Note that the phrase “to them” has been supplied in the translation to clarify what is meant.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 犹大人攻打耶路撒冷，将城攻取，用刀杀了城内的人，并且放火烧城。
verses.en: The men of Judah attacked Jerusalem and captured it. They put the sword to it and set the city on fire.

verses.zh: 后来犹大人下去，与住山地、南地，和高原的迦南人争战。
verses.en: Later the men of Judah went down to attack the Canaanites living in the hill country, the Negev,[NOTE:1] and the foothills.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Negev is the area of central, southern Judah, south of the hill country and Beer Sheba and west of the rift valley.
The foothills (שְׁפֵלָה, shephelah) are the region between the Judean hill country and the Mediterranean coastal plain.

verses.zh: 犹大人去攻击住希伯仑的迦南人，杀了示筛、亚希幔、挞买。希伯仑从前名叫基列・亚巴。
verses.en: The men of Judah attacked the Canaanites living in Hebron. (Hebron used to be called Kiriath Arba.) They killed Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

verses.zh: 他们从那里去攻击底壁的居民；底壁从前名叫基列・西弗。
verses.en: From there they attacked the people of Debir.[NOTE:1] (Debir used to be called Kiriath Sepher.)
notes: Heb “they went from there against the inhabitants of Debir.” The LXX reads the verb as “they went up,” which suggests that the Hebrew text translated by the LXX read וַיַּעַל (vayyaʿal) rather than the MT’s וַיֵּלֶךְ (vayyelekh). It is possible that this is the text to be preferred in v. 11. Cf. Josh 15:15.

verses.zh: 迦勒说：「谁能攻打基列・西弗，将城夺取，我就把我女儿押撒给他为妻。」
verses.en: Caleb said, “To the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher I will give my daughter Achsah as a wife.”

verses.zh: 迦勒兄弟基纳斯的儿子俄陀聂夺取了那城，迦勒就把女儿押撒给他为妻。
verses.en: When Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother,[NOTE:1] captured it, Caleb[NOTE:2] gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
notes: “Caleb’s younger brother” may refer to Othniel or to Kenaz (in which case Othniel was Caleb’s nephew; so CEV).
Heb “he”; the referent (Caleb) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 押撒过门的时候，劝丈夫向她父亲求一块田。押撒一下驴，迦勒问她说：「你要甚么？」
verses.en: One time Achsah[NOTE:1] came and charmed her father[NOTE:2] so she could ask him for some land. When she got down from her donkey, Caleb said to her, “What would you like?”
notes: Heb “she”; the referent (Achsah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “him.” The pronoun could refer to Othniel, in which case one would translate, “she incited him [Othniel] to ask her father for a field.” This is problematic, however, for Achsah, not Othniel, makes the request in v. 15. The LXX has “he [Othniel] urged her to ask her father for a field.” This appears to be an attempt to reconcile the apparent inconsistency and probably does not reflect the original text. If Caleb is understood as the referent of the pronoun, the problem disappears. For a fuller discussion of the issue, see P. G. Mosca, “Who Seduced Whom? A Note on Joshua 15:18 // Judges 1:14, ” CBQ 46 (1984): 18-22. The translation takes Caleb to be the referent, specified as “her father.”

verses.zh: 她说：「求你赐福给我，你既将我安置在南地，求你也给我水泉。」迦勒就把上泉下泉赐给她。
verses.en: She answered, “Please give me a special present.[NOTE:1] Since you have given me land in the Negev, now give me springs of water.” So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs.[NOTE:2]
notes: Elsewhere the Hebrew word בְרָכָה (verakhah) is often translated “blessing,” but here it refers to a gift (as in Gen 33:11; 1 Sam 25:27; 30:26; 2 Kgs 5:15).
Some translations regard the expressions “springs of water” (גֻּלֹּת מָיִם, gullot mayim) and “springs” (גֻּלֹּת) as place names here (cf. NRSV).

verses.zh: 摩西的内兄（或译：岳父）是基尼人，他的子孙与犹大人一同离了棕树城，往亚拉得以南的犹大旷野去，就住在民中。
verses.en: Now the descendants of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law, went up with the people of Judah from the city of date palm trees[NOTE:1] to Arad in the wilderness of Judah,[NOTE:2] located in the Negev.[NOTE:3] They went and lived with the people of Judah.[NOTE:4]
notes: The city of date palm trees refers to Jericho. See Deut 34:3.
Part of the Greek ms tradition lacks the words “of Judah.”
Heb “[to] the wilderness of Judah in the Negev, Arad.”

The phrase “of Judah” is supplied here in the translation. Some ancient textual witnesses read, “They went and lived with the Amalekites.” This reading, however, is probably influenced by 1 Sam 15:6 (see also Num 24:20-21).

verses.zh: 犹大和他哥哥西缅同去，击杀了住洗法的迦南人，将城尽行毁灭，那城的名便叫何珥玛。
verses.en: The men of Judah went with their brothers the men of Simeon[NOTE:1] and defeated the Canaanites living in Zephath. They wiped out Zephath.[NOTE:2] So people now call the city Hormah.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Judah went with Simeon, his brother.”
Heb “it”; the referent (the city of Zephath) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The name Hormah (חָרְמָה, khormah) sounds like the Hebrew verb translated “wipe out” (חָרַם, kharam).

verses.zh: 犹大又取了迦萨和迦萨的四境，亚实基伦和亚实基伦的四境，以革伦和以革伦的四境。
verses.en: The men of Judah captured Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the territory surrounding each of these cities.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “The men of Judah captured Gaza and its surrounding territory, Ashkelon and its surrounding territory, and Ekron and its surrounding territory.”

verses.zh: 耶和华与犹大同在，犹大就赶出山地的居民，只是不能赶出平原的居民，因为他们有铁车。
verses.en: The Lord was with the men of Judah. They conquered[NOTE:1] the hill country, but they could not[NOTE:2] conquer the people living in the coastal plain because they had chariots with iron-rimmed wheels.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “seized possession of”; or “occupied.”
Several textual witnesses support the inclusion of this verb.

Regarding the translation “chariots with iron-rimmed wheels,” see Y. Yadin, The Art of Warfare in Biblical Lands, 255, and the article by R. Drews, “The ‘Chariots of Iron’ of Joshua and Judges,” JSOT 45 (1989): 15-23.

verses.zh: 以色列人照摩西所说的，将希伯仑给了迦勒；迦勒就从那里赶出亚衲族的三个族长。
verses.en: Caleb received[NOTE:1] Hebron, just as Moses had promised. He drove out the three Anakites.
notes: Heb “they gave to Caleb.”

verses.zh: 便雅悯人没有赶出住耶路撒冷的耶布斯人。耶布斯人仍在耶路撒冷与便雅悯人同住，直到今日。
verses.en: The men of Benjamin, however, did not conquer the Jebusites living in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] The Jebusites live with the people of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this very day.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
The statement to this very day reflects the perspective of the author, who must have written prior to David’s conquest of the Jebusites (see 2 Sam 5:6-7).

verses.zh: 约瑟家也上去攻打伯特利；耶和华与他们同在。
verses.en: When the men[NOTE:1] of Joseph attacked[NOTE:2] Bethel,[NOTE:3] the Lord was with them.
notes: Heb “house.” This is a metonymy for the warriors from the tribe.
Heb “went up.”
For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

verses.zh: 约瑟家打发人去窥探伯特利（那城起先名叫路斯）。
verses.en: When the men of Joseph spied out Bethel (it used to be called Luz),

verses.zh: 窥探的人看见一个人从城里出来，就对他说：「求你将进城的路指示我们，我们必恩待你。」
verses.en: the spies spotted[NOTE:1] a man leaving the city. They said to him, “If you show us a secret entrance into the city, we will reward you.”
notes: Heb “saw.”

verses.zh: 那人将进城的路指示他们，他们就用刀击杀了城中的居民，但将那人和他全家放去。
verses.en: He showed them a secret entrance into the city, and they put the city to the sword. But they let the man and his extended family leave safely.

verses.zh: 那人往赫人之地去，筑了一座城，起名叫路斯。那城到如今还叫这名。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] moved to Hittite country and built a city. He named it Luz, and it has kept that name to this very day.
notes: Heb “the man.”

verses.zh: 玛拿西没有赶出伯・善和属伯・善乡村的居民，他纳和属他纳乡村的居民，多珥和属多珥乡村的居民，以伯莲和属以伯莲乡村的居民，米吉多和属米吉多乡村的居民；迦南人却执意住在那些地方。
verses.en: The men of Manasseh did not conquer Beth Shean, Taanach, or their surrounding towns. Nor did they conquer the people living in Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo,[NOTE:1] or their surrounding towns.[NOTE:2] The Canaanites managed[NOTE:3] to remain in those areas.[NOTE:4]
notes: For location see Map1-D4; Map2-C1; Map4-C2; Map5-F2; Map7-B1.

Heb “The men of Manasseh did not conquer Beth Shean and its surrounding towns, Taanach and its surrounding towns, the people living in Dor and its surrounding towns, the people living in Ibleam and its surrounding towns, or the people living in Megiddo and its surrounding towns.”
Or “were determined.”
Heb “in this land.”

verses.zh: 及至以色列强盛了，就使迦南人做苦工，没有把他们全然赶出。
verses.en: Whenever Israel was strong militarily, they forced the Canaanites to do hard labor, but they never totally conquered them.

verses.zh: 以法莲没有赶出住基色的迦南人。于是迦南人仍住在基色，在以法莲中间。
verses.en: The men of Ephraim did not conquer the Canaanites living in Gezer. The Canaanites lived among them in Gezer.

verses.zh: 西布伦没有赶出基伦的居民和拿哈拉的居民。于是迦南人仍住在西布伦中间，成了服苦的人。
verses.en: The men of Zebulun did not conquer the people living in Kitron and Nahalol.[NOTE:1] The Canaanites lived among them and were forced to do hard labor.
notes: Heb “the people living in Kitron and the people living in Nahalol.”

verses.zh: 亚设没有赶出亚柯和西顿的居民，亚黑拉和亚革悉的居民，黑巴、亚弗革与利合的居民。
verses.en: The men of Asher did not conquer the people living in Acco or Sidon,[NOTE:1] nor did they conquer Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphek, or Rehob.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.
Heb “The men of Asher did not conquer the people living in Acco, the people living in Sidon, Ahlab, Acco, Helbah, Aphek, or Rehob.”

verses.zh: 于是，亚设因为没有赶出那地的迦南人，就住在他们中间。
verses.en: The people of Asher live among the Canaanites residing in the land because they did not conquer them.

verses.zh: 拿弗他利没有赶出伯・示麦和伯・亚纳的居民，于是拿弗他利就住在那地的迦南人中间；然而伯・示麦和伯・亚纳的居民成了服苦的人。
verses.en: The men of Naphtali did not conquer the people living in Beth Shemesh or Beth Anath.[NOTE:1] They live among the Canaanites residing in the land. The Canaanites[NOTE:2] living in Beth Shemesh and Beth Anath were forced to do hard labor for them.
notes: Heb “the people living in Beth Shemesh or the people living in Beth Anath.”
The term “Canaanites” is supplied here both for clarity and for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 亚摩利人强逼但人住在山地，不容他们下到平原；
verses.en: The Amorites forced the people of Dan to live in the hill country. They did not allow them to live in[NOTE:1] the coastal plain.
notes: Heb “come down into.”

verses.zh: 亚摩利人却执意住在希烈山和亚雅伦并沙宾。然而约瑟家胜了他们，使他们成了服苦的人。
verses.en: The Amorites managed[NOTE:1] to remain in Har Heres,[NOTE:2] Aijalon, and Shaalbim. Whenever the tribe of Joseph was strong militarily,[NOTE:3] the Amorites were forced to do hard labor.
notes: Or “were determined.”
Or “Mount Heres”; the term הַר (har) means “mount” or “mountain” in Hebrew.
Heb “Whenever the hand of the tribe of Joseph was heavy.”

verses.zh: 亚摩利人的境界，是从亚克拉滨坡，从西拉而上。
verses.en: The border of Amorite territory ran from the Scorpion Ascent[NOTE:1] to Sela and on up.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “the Ascent of Scorpions” (עַקְרַבִּים [ʿaqrabbim] means “scorpions” in Hebrew).
Or “Amorite territory started at the Pass of the Scorpions at Sela and then went on up.”
